security_audit.summary: Adjudicated 265 static findings against the agent-browser skill, which consists of Markdown documentation and example/template shell scripts wrapping the 'belt'/'infsh' CLI for Playwright browser automation. Every finding is a false positive: shell command substitutions capture CLI output into variables with hardcoded literal arguments, 'hardcoded URLs' are example.com/docs placeholders, 'path traversal' matches are relative Markdown links, and the credential-handling examples actually teach secure practices (secrets managers, no logging). No data exfiltration, command injection, or prompt injection was found.

remediation.issue: Documentation shows a plaintext example password ('password123') inline in a login flow.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the literal example password with a clearly non-secret placeholder such as $PASSWORD and reference the existing secrets-manager guidance so readers never copy a real-looking credential.

remediation.issue: Several examples run 'execute' with arbitrary JavaScript on the page.
remediation.suggestion: Add a short note that the 'execute' function runs untrusted JavaScript in the page context and should only be used with code the operator controls, to reinforce safe usage.

1. **Open** - Navigate to URL, get `@e` refs for elements
| `open` | Navigate to URL, configure browser (viewport, proxy, video recording) |
| `snapshot` | Re-fetch page state with `@e` refs after DOM changes |
| `interact` | Perform actions using `@e` refs (click, fill, drag, upload, etc.) |
| `screenshot` | Take page screenshot (viewport or full page) |
| `execute` | Run JavaScript code on the page |
| `close` | Close session, returns video if recording was enabled |

content.user_title: Automate Web Browsing for AI Agents
content.value_statement: AI agents cannot reliably interact with live websites that require clicking, typing, and navigation. This skill gives agents a simple element-reference system to open pages, fill forms, take screenshots, run JavaScript, and record video through the inference.sh CLI.
actual_capabilities: Open web pages and receive numbered element references (@e refs) for every interactive element.
Perform interactions: click, double-click, fill, type, press keys, select dropdowns, hover, check, drag-and-drop, and file upload.
Take viewport or full-page screenshots and record session video for debugging or demos.
Run custom JavaScript on the page and read the returned result.
Persist state across a session and route traffic through an HTTP or SOCKS proxy with authentication.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh 'belt' CLI to be installed and an active login; it does not run standalone.
Element @e refs are invalidated after navigation, so the page must be re-snapshotted after any change.
It automates a browser but does not include CAPTCHA solving or built-in anti-bot evasion.
Credential handling is left to the operator; the skill provides guidance but stores no secrets.

use_cases.title: Extract structured data from a website
use_cases.description: Open a target page, snapshot its elements, run JavaScript or read element text, and capture screenshots to collect content for downstream analysis.

use_cases.title: Automate a login and form workflow
use_cases.description: Fill in credentials, submit a login form, verify the authenticated page, then complete a multi-step form using stable element references.

use_cases.title: Record a browser session as video
use_cases.description: Enable video recording when opening a session to produce a replay of every action for debugging or product demos.

prompt_templates.title: Open a page and list elements
prompt_templates.prompt: Open https://example.com with agent-browser and tell me the interactive elements you can see.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: first interaction with a page

prompt_templates.title: Fill and submit a form
prompt_templates.prompt: Using agent-browser, open the contact form at https://example.com/contact, fill the name and email fields, type a message, and submit it.

prompt_templates.title: Extract data with a screenshot
prompt_templates.prompt: Open the product page with agent-browser, take a full-page screenshot, and extract the product titles and prices from the page.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: content extraction plus visual capture

prompt_templates.title: Authenticated session through a proxy with video
prompt_templates.prompt: Open a recorded agent-browser session through my configured proxy, log in with the provided credentials, confirm the dashboard loaded, then close the session and give me the video.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: proxy, authentication, and recording combined

output_examples.input: Open https://example.com and list the interactive elements.
output_examples.output: Opened the page and found five interactive elements: a Home link, a search input, a Submit button, a Choose option dropdown, and an Agree checkbox. Each has a reference you can act on.

output_examples.input: Fill the login form and sign in.
output_examples.output: Filled the email and password fields, clicked Sign In, and re-snapshotted the page. The URL changed away from the login route and a Dashboard element is now visible, so login succeeded.

output_examples.input: Record a session and return the video after closing.
output_examples.output: Opened a session with video recording enabled, performed the requested actions, and closed the session. A video file of the full session was returned for review.

best_practices: Re-snapshot the page after any click, form submission, or dynamic load so element references stay valid.
Store credentials in a secrets manager or environment variable and never log passwords; the authentication reference shows the recommended pattern.
Always close the session when finished, ideally with a trap, to release the browser and avoid leaking state.
anti_patterns: Reusing an @e reference after the page has navigated, which leads to failed or misdirected actions.
Hardcoding real passwords directly into scripts instead of reading them from a secure source.
Enabling video recording while handling sensitive data, since the recording may capture credentials on screen.

faq.question: What do I need to install to use this skill?
faq.answer: You need the inference.sh 'belt' CLI installed and to run 'belt login' before opening sessions. Installation instructions are linked in the skill.

faq.question: What are @e refs?
faq.answer: They are numbered references to interactive elements on the page, such as @e1 or @e2. You use them to target clicks, text entry, and other actions.

faq.question: Why do my element references stop working?
faq.answer: References are invalidated whenever the page navigates or its content changes. Run a snapshot again to get fresh references before continuing.

faq.question: Can it run custom JavaScript on a page?
faq.answer: Yes. The execute function runs JavaScript you provide in the page context and returns the result. Only use code you control and trust.

faq.question: Does it support proxies?
faq.answer: Yes. You can supply an HTTP or SOCKS proxy URL with optional username and password when opening a session to route the browser traffic through it.

faq.question: How do I keep credentials safe?
faq.answer: Read credentials from an environment variable or a secrets manager, never log them, and close the session when finished. The authentication reference documents these practices.
